shortDescription: Ireland's services sector expanded in September as demand strengthened and new business grew at its fastest pace in 10 months, a business survey showed on Monday.

children: Ireland's services sector expanded in September as demand strengthened and new business grew at its fastest pace in 10 months, a business survey showed on Monday.
The AIB Ireland Services Business Activity Index, compiled by S&P Global, fell to 54.1 from 55.4 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction.

New business rose for a fifth straight month and at the strongest rate since November 2025. Export business also increased for a fifth month, but only marginally, with Business Services the only sector to record a decline.
Capacity pressures intensified as outstanding work increased for a fourth consecutive month, and at the fastest pace since August 2024.
Employment returned to growth after August's pause, although the pace of hiring was described as relatively weak.

Cost pressures strengthened, with input price inflation accelerating to its highest since May, driven by wages and higher fuel and energy costs. Prices charged rose at the sharpest rate in five months and were the second-strongest in nearly two-and-a-half years.
Business confidence improved for a sixth straight month to its highest since February 2025, linked to planned investment, new contracts and marketing efforts.

"New business continued to grow strongly following a dip in activity earlier in the year, although new export business growth eased on the month. Higher activity was driven by new clients and marketing efforts," said David McNamara, AIB Chief Economist.
